findings.title: Max in parts never checks the named tokens are held: a quantity above what the spendable UTxOs hold sends a partial Max that leaves the ADA, blaming tokens (or is refused as 'not enough ADA')
findings.scenario: Private Send to a Seedelf with Max on and a token T at its full held amount. The form's held figure is unlocked(balances.seedelf), which keeps UTxOs reserved by a chain being sent: a Lovejoin return's merge target (a session's funding change) or a payment's waiting parts. readContract leaves those UTxOs out of `utxos`. Say the request's utxos are H (10 T, about 2.2 ₳) and 25 UTxOs of 10 ₳ ADA alone, while R (5 T) is reserved, and the ask is T: 15. Part 1: share_of caps at 10, so `more` is true and keep_ada limits the picks to H. It pays about 1.9 ₳ + 10 T. Part 2: no holder of T is left, share is empty and `more` is still true, so at_most = 0 and the picks are empty. fit_part bails with a plain error ('Not enough ADA in the Seedelf balance…', not a NotEnough). max_in_parts treats that as 'a part failed for anything but its fee': no chain is tried, Max returns the one part, left = 25 and left_why = Tokens. The review shows Max paying about 1.9 ₳ + 10 T and says '25 private UTxOs stay for another payment: each holds a token that won't fit in one output with the rest'. 250 ₳ of ADA-only UTxOs are left behind, with a false reason. If all of T is reserved, Max is refused: the worker maps the bail to 'Not enough ADA in your private balance…' while 250 ₳ is spendable. One-transaction Max refused both cases in words through core's `holding`: 'The Seedelf balance holds only 10 of the token …, not 15'. No money is lost: the review shows what is built.
findings.since: web-wallet/1.6.0 (1cd50dba: share_of-based max_in_parts; the bail's words and LeftWhy came in the 1.6.0 review)
findings.evidence: lib.rs:4633-4646 build_transfer_parts' Max path calls max_in_parts directly: no assets_of or holding check of only.tokens against request.utxos (in_parts is covered by the first one-transaction try, lib.rs:4647, whose core select_script_inputs runs holding first, build.rs:2558). lib.rs:3983-3994 share_of caps at what the group holds; lib.rs:3997-4012 `less` keeps the remainder. lib.rs:4054-4058 `more = !less(tokens,&share).is_empty()` → keep_ada; lib.rs:3924-3929 at_most = (group.len()+ada).min(k) = 0 with no holder. lib.rs:4062-4064 `if picks.is_empty() { bail!("Not enough ADA in the Seedelf balance for this payment and its fees") }` is an adhoc anyhow error, so build::is_short (build.rs:2869, downcast NotEnough) is false. lib.rs:4484-4488 failed = Some(e); break. lib.rs:4500-4504 why = Tokens; lib.rs:4509-4538: not short, so no max_chained; parts non-empty, so no Err. lib.rs:4543-4551 left/why go on the last part. Before parts: lib.rs:3113-3116 transfer_spend → build::max_inputs → build.rs:2915 holding → build.rs:2968-2975 'holds only … not …'. UI: Transfer.tsx:106 recipientAmounts(network, seedelf.tokens, …) with seedelf = free.seedelf = unlocked(balances.seedelf) (Home.tsx:223,714; format.ts:376-384 subtracts only coin-control locks). balances.ts:316 seedelf side = spendableOwned less spent (reserved included). script-spend.ts:237-243 readContract drops reserved (sending chains) from utxos. TokenAmounts.tsx:37-39 a token's max is the held figure. short.ts:23,80-88: PRIVATE_SHORT matches the bail; with Max (asked null) the 'plain' sentence. en.json withdraw.leftTokens_other: "each holds a token that won't fit in one output with the rest." The test a verifier could write (seedelf-wasm tests/r51_w1a_1.rs, helpers copied from api_test's parts_of_any_shape): utxos = [utxo(1, 1_000_000, &[T:10])] + ada(100, 25, 10_000_000); `api::build_transfer(sk, transfer(utxos.clone(), None, vec![T:15]))` errs 'holds only 10'. `api::build_transfer_parts(sk, transfer(utxos, None, vec![T:15]))` today returns Ok: 1 part, left 25, left_why Some(Tokens), payments[0].tokens quantity "10". Expected: refused in words, as one transaction's Max was.
findings.fix: Validate Max's token list up front, as one-transaction Max did, in both Max paths (build_transfer_parts' and build_withdraw_parts' `most`, lib.rs:4633 and 4764). Run assets_of over only.tokens (zero, malformed and duplicate entries), then check each token's u128 total in request.utxos against it, and refuse in core's words ('The Seedelf balance holds only X of the token …'), which the worker passes through. Never read fit_part's empty-pick bail as LeftWhy::Tokens: give it its own error, and keep Tokens for too_much and fitting. The class's other half is in TS: the private Send form offers, as a token's max, held tokens that readContract won't let a spend use (reserved by a chain being sent). Either subtract them as `unlocked` subtracts coin-control locks, or say they're held by a payment still going.
findings.owner_why: The fix either restores a refusal in the parts path (one transaction's Max refused this), or sends what the spendable UTxOs hold and says so, which changes what Max offers. The owner picks one. Changing the form's token max also changes what a screen offers.
findings.known_check: Searched docs/backlog.md and docs/archive/plans/*.md for 'holds only', 'phantom', 'more than held', 'leftWhy', 'LeftWhy', "won't fit", 'reserved', 'returning' with Max, and 'named token'. Found only chunk-34's 321-parts-worker#6 (why Max left UTxOs, about fees, limit and fitting tokens) and chunk-12 #18 (a token box refuses more than the balance holds). Neither covers a Max ask above the spendable UTxOs' holdings. It is not among 1.9.1's Left open (picking's biggest holder, r2-planner#1, tests#1) or 1.9.1/1.9.0's Not fixed.

guards.stops: A funding's or a carry's amount being retried on the 20 largest UTxOs (merging other sessions' money; a carry spending more than given)
An amount going out as more than MAX_PARTS transactions
Several recipients (not a funding) being split into parts
Each part's UTxOs, carries included: ours, no Seedelf, evaluable (check_spendable runs in every per-part build)
A carry read back from an output that isn't it: refused when none or two outputs could be the carry

checked_ok: No misdirection: every part pays payments[0].to or the recipient's register. Carries go to a fresh re-randomization of the owner (ScriptSpend::carry → pay_rest Seedelf(change_owner)), and change goes back to the owner.

A funding's beside payments (the 5 ₳ collateral) go only in the plan's or the chain's first part (with's `first && funding`, chained's `starts`). paid_of counts payments[0] alone. holding_enough and Worth::apart's owed include beside, and reserving's owed excludes it consistently.

No plan underpays. in_parts and chained end only when tokens are empty and owed is 0, or when the last amount pays owed.max(least(tokens)). So reserving's second plan, which wins on `takes <`, can't pay less than asked or drop a token.

Max chains always spend their carries: max_chained returns Ok only via the last part over carry + rest (fewer than 20), which max_inputs takes whole, the carry being ADA alone and always fitting. Amount chains' unspent carries are counted by carry_kept, so no carry is uncounted.

Result figures match the built transactions. Amounts: Paid is lovelace raised to the least, paid exactly by pay_address/deposit_outputs. Most: rest_lovelace. Everything: change_lovelace to the address. Carry parts: the tokens' least, or 0. whole() sums payments[0], fees and change (kept carries included), and a carry spent later is counted nowhere, which is correct.

Sums: reserving, taken and carry_kept use checked_add. Token totals (quantity_of, token_group, share_of, less) are u128. The beside sum is at most 20 × MAX_SUPPLY. holding_enough's u64 is the rule's named exception.
MAX_PARTS bounds: in_parts at most 25 parts, chained at most 24 in all, max_in_parts at most 25. `MAX_PARTS - 1 - anchor` can't underflow (anchor ≤ 24) and `MAX_PARTS - anchor` is at least 1.
fit_part's loop terminates: k and h only decrease, ada rises at most to min(free, k − holders), and Room::fewer/after return None at the floor.
is_short classification: core's NotEnough. Amounts are raised to their least, so pay_address's and payment_outputs' plain errors and deposit_outputs' TooLittle can't arise for parts.
Every part's request.utxos, the carry row included, runs check_spendable. The carry's register is a re-randomization of ours, holds no Seedelf and no reference script, and its datum is within depth.

Amount parts can't see phantom tokens: the first one-transaction try runs core's holding over `fits` before any TooMany, and Worth::apart's alone subset is chosen only where its rows hold every token.
Paid and SeedelfPaid serialize minimum None as null, which whole()'s `!== null` check relies on.
Settled, not re-reported: the Seedelf minimum is sized on a dummy base address, about 0.12 ₳ an output high (chunk 34, call 9: stays, a wallet-wide and CLI change).
notes: Worth::of's first key is always `true` (lib.rs:3713), where Worth::apart's is `adds > 0` (lib.rs:3819), against the struct's own doc ('whether it adds anything'). With a funding's histories, the `worth` fallback ranks by purpose first, so a better-ranked UTxO adding nothing comes before an ADA-rich one of a worse rank: a stranger's token bundle reads as 'received', rank 1 for a funding, ahead of own money at rank 4. Only by_history_first's fallbacks use it, after the history order fails or chains. I traced no concrete refusal or extra cost. It's a doubt for the planner's owner.

Worth::apart's per-class `total` (lib.rs:3772) is a plain u64 `.sum()` of rows' ADA, only compared and sorted. As with holding_enough, a wrap needs a lying index, which is out of scope. CLAUDE.md's overflow rule names only holding_enough and Holdings::spare as such sums. u128 would match the rule, as core's apart does.

An amount chain's carry part always pays the recipient at least an output's least, since Some(0) is raised in transfer_plan and amounts_of. In an ADA-only stretch, the part where what's owed ends under that least pays up to one least over. api_test's an_amount_the_balance_cant_pay_is_refused_never_paid_in_part documents carries paying their least. I take this as the r2-planner#1 family, not a new finding.

build::carried (build.rs:2259-2269) could see two candidate outputs in a transfer chain's ADA-only carry part if the recipient's payment (an ADA-only least) equals the carry exactly. That is refused as non-short. It needs the carry to land exactly at its least, so the odds are negligible.

in_parts' anchor loop breaks on the first non-short chain error (lib.rs:4235, `Err(_) => break`). A chain that runs out of room from the latest anchor stops earlier anchors being tried. It's a design choice, and I traced no feasible payment it refuses.

w1a#1's class also covers zero, malformed or duplicate entries in a Max ask. share_of and less parse with unwrap_or(0) and drop them silently, and duplicates count twice in share_of, where one transaction's assets_of refused or merged them. The UI never sends them. Validating with assets_of up front, as in w1a#1's fix, closes them.

Performance, not a finding: core's one_more tries every ADA-only single of strictly increasing value. A stranger who pays thousands of distinct-amount dust UTxOs makes an amount's last-part attempts slow, at the stranger's own heavy cost, which the user receives. The backlog already has the history-first planner's 25 s refusals.
